outputs: summaries with varying style features such as abstractiveness, specificity, length, and readability

changes_made.explanation: Normalized dataset names to standard forms (CNN/DailyMail instead of CNN, Newsroom instead of NEWSROOM, XSum instead of XSUM) and model name (HydraSum instead of HYDRASUM)

Normalized metric names to standard forms and removed duplicates. All ROUGE variants (R1/R2/RL) are simplified to ROUGE. Speciteller is the tool used to measure specificity, so it's normalized to just 'Specificity'.
No LLMs were used as judges in this paper. The paper uses human evaluation and automatic metrics, but no LLM-based evaluation.

guideline: Workers rated summaries on 5-point Likert scale for relevance, coherence, grammaticality, and binary factual/non-factual for factuality

changes_made.explanation: Normalized 'grammatically' to 'grammaticality' and consolidated guideline descriptions

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper focuses on text summarization with style control, using both automatic metrics and human evaluation. No LLM-based evaluation was conducted. The main contributions are the HydraSum architecture and its ability to disentangle style features in summarization.
